expected.tagline: All Walls Must Fall is a Tech-Noir Tactics game set in Berlin 2089, where the Cold War never ended.
expected.description:
Berlin, November 2089: The Cold War never ended. For 150 years both sides have used time manipulation technology to observe and counter each other’s every move. Now this fragile state of affairs is approaching a breaking point, as a rogue nuclear strike will send the world into turmoil. Both sides have scrambled to send agents back in time to find who is behind the attack and how to prevent it. If they fail, the whole world will turn to ash, forever.

All Walls Must Fall is an isometric tactics game where actions happen to the pulsing beat of the music. You control time travelling secret agents as they jump and loop through a single night in the city of Berlin. Using a pausable real-time system, carefully plan your decisions and use powerful time manipulation abilities to your advantage, as you carry out your mission in the shadows or in plain sight. Levels are procedurally recombined, giving All Walls Must Fall a highly replayable campaign structure, while still offering individually crafted components and set-pieces.

All Walls Must Fall takes inspiration from genre classics like X-Com, Syndicate and REZ, as well more recent indie games like The Banner Saga, Braid, SUPERHOT and Crypt of the Necrodancer.

Isometric action-tactics game for Windows, Mac and Linux
Hybrid real-time / simultaneous turn-based tactical gameplay
Procedurally generated levels and campaign that plays different every time
Sci-Fi noir Berlin as a divided city in which the Cold War never ended
Mind-bending time manipulation abilities that allow you to experiment with possible futures and rewind to the past.
Synaesthetic nightclub environments and audio
A simulation sandbox featuring crowd simulation and destructible objects
NEW GAME+ mode that allows you to keep upgrading your gear as you increase the challenge - forever
A parable that reflects on free will, moral ambiguity and the meaning of freedom
Developed by a team of former AAA professionals using Unreal Engine 4Original Soundtrack
All Walls Must Fall features a killer soundtrack that reacts to the gameplay, and features original music from talented artists drawn from both the Berlin club scene and the world of video game music:

Jukio Kallio (minit, Nuclear Throne, LUFTRAUSERS)
Ben Prunty (FTL, Darkside Detective, Into the Breach)
Kuedo (Blade Runner Black Out 2022, Knives, Planet Mu)
The Orion Correlation and Lost & Found (Voidance records)
Mona Mur (Kane & Lynch 2: Dog Days, Velvet Assassin)

installSteps.text: Alternatively, download All Walls Must Fall - A Tech-Noir Tactics Game directly from the official site at http://www.inbetweengames.com/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.
All Walls Must Fall - A Tech-Noir Tactics Game is also on Steam and is free there. Open the store page and press Play Game to add it to your library.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Check your distribution's package manager first, which is usually the easiest route. Otherwise download the AppImage from the official site, mark it executable and run it.

Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. All Walls Must Fall - A Tech-Noir Tactics Game needs roughly 2.0 GB of free disk space.

set.tagline: One Berlin night, endless second chances, and every nightclub floor a tactical problem.
set.description: All Walls Must Fall is a permanently free, single-player tactics game set in an alternate 2089 Berlin. Pause and rewind nightclub encounters, plan around crowds and cover, and work through a campaign whose levels recombine authored pieces. Available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Steam itself now requires Windows 10 or later. macOS: 10.12.6 or later, dual-core Intel CPU, 4 GB RAM, Metal graphics, 2 GB storage. Linux: 64-bit OS, dual-core Intel CPU, 4 GB RAM, OpenGL 4.3 graphics, 2 GB storage.

qualityBar.verdict: A nightclub shootout turns into a puzzle you can rewind, revise, and finally perform to the beat.

set.longDescription:
Berlin, 2089. The Cold War is still going, the music is loud, and someone is about to set off a bomb that changes everything. In All Walls Must Fall, you are sent back through one night to find the people behind it. The premise sounds like a thriller, but the real pleasure is in the minute-to-minute tactics: entering a crowded club, reading a room, and deciding how much trouble to cause before anyone notices you.

Time is your most useful piece of equipment. Actions unfold to the music, yet you can pause to plan and rewind when a move turns ugly. A risky route across a dance floor can become a careful sequence of shots, cover, and repositioning. The game lets you try a future, see its cost, and pull the decision apart. That makes a failed encounter feel less like a dead end and more like a draft you can improve. When a plan finally works, it can look surprisingly effortless, even if getting there took several attempts.

The levels are recombined from authored pieces. You are not simply memorizing a fixed corridor and repeating the same solution. Crowds move, sight lines matter, and destructible scenery can change where it is safe to stand. The club setting does more than give the game neon color: its pulse gives the tactics a rhythm, while the bodies on the floor make even a small mistake conspicuous. The soundtrack draws from several artists, including Jukio Kallio and Ben Prunty, and reacts to what is happening on screen.

There is a campaign to work through and a New Game+ mode if you want to keep pushing your equipment and decisions. The story circles questions about control and freedom, but it does not ask you to sit still for them. You keep moving between conversation, infiltration, and the moment an imperfect plan becomes a firefight. That mixture can be messy. It is also what makes the game more interesting than a neat set of isolated combat arenas.

This is a single-player game for Windows, macOS, and Linux. The developer made it permanently free on Steam and itch.io in 2024. Steam handles installation; no separate launcher, server, or multiplayer party is needed. The published storage requirement is 2 GB across platforms. Native controller support is not clearly documented in the current store listing, so PlayBound does not claim a verified controller profile for it yet. If you want a tactical game where changing your mind is a mechanic instead of a reload-screen confession, this night in Berlin is worth entering.
set.whyWePickedIt: We picked All Walls Must Fall because rewinding a bad move changes how you think about a tactical fight. The club is a place to scout, negotiate, and improvise, while the beat keeps the whole operation moving. Its permanent free release makes a distinctive, complete single-player game easy to try.
set.thatOneThing: The dance floor lets you rewind a botched gunfight until it looks like you meant to do that.

installSteps.text: Open the official Steam page or the developer's itch.io page. The game is permanently free on both stores.
On Steam, select Play Game and let Steam install the Windows build. Launch it from your library after the download finishes.
Select the macOS build on the official store page, install it through that store, and launch it from your library. The developer lists macOS 10.12.6 or later.
Select the Linux build on the official store page and install it through that store. The developer lists a 64-bit system with OpenGL 4.3 support.

firstPlaySteps.text: Start the campaign, try the pause and rewind controls in the first encounter, and check the game's key bindings before a longer run.

bestFor: Tactical players who enjoy revising a plan mid-fight
Single-player campaigns with a strong soundtrack
Anyone curious about a free game with a complete beginning and end
notFor: Players looking for co-op or online matches
Anyone who wants verified plug-and-play controller support

faq.q: Is All Walls Must Fall free?

faq.q: Does it work with a controller?
faq.a: PlayBound has not verified a native controller mode or a PlayBound Controls profile for this game yet. Keyboard and mouse are the safe choice.

faq.q: How much storage do I need?
faq.a: The developer lists 2 GB of free storage for Windows, macOS, and Linux. This is an install-space requirement, not a measured download size.
